attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No certified values are yet available for the seven endpoint source evaluations, the uniform M_8 bound, or the endpoint tail tau_end in the continuum scaling window.
steps: Contract the already-known Feshbach null vector into the endpoint plaquette incidences before forming any endpoint spectrum; the relevant Yang-Mills object becomes the scalar connected cumulant kappa_{4,v}^{sing}(eta_v).

Use log Z_v rather than Z_v. This removes disconnected Wick-square terms from the fourth cumulant; the remaining Gaussian source response is quadratic and is annihilated by the fourth derivative stencil.

Check the local nonabelian commutator contact: on every straight boundary edge the oriented null incidence sum is zero, so the f^{ACD}f^{BCD} straight contact contributes no scalar endpoint weight. Only endpoint/corner boxes and tails remain.

Replace the previous five-point fourth difference by the seven-point stencil with coefficients (-1/6,2,-13/2,28/3,-13/2,2,-1/6). Its moment equations kill powers 0,2,6, all odd powers by symmetry, and normalize the fourth power to one.
Taylor expansion gives the certified error coefficient 7/240 h^4 M_8, improving the crude h^2 M_6 endpoint uncertainty and making an actual interval test plausible.
Sum the certified endpoint intervals with the color prefactor (g_a^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 and the Holder/cluster tail interval, then compare M_G+I_R with zero.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The algebraic cancellation and finite-difference certificate are valid, but promotion needs actual endpoint-box data or a sharp analytic character/cluster bound proving that the certified interval stays above -M_G.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Endpoint kappa_4 scalar certificate for the post-H,K Wilson collar term

assumptions: Regulator is the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator with a << sqrt(t_a) << r_end, and endpoint boxes are disjoint after the chosen collar localization.
The Feshbach null vector has already been fixed from the H,K block; eta_v is its induced oriented color-singlet incidence on endpoint plaquette sheets.
For each endpoint box, L_{v,a}(s;eta_v) is real and C^8 for |s| <= 3h with bound M_{8,v}(3h).
The straight-edge incidence identity holds for every non-corner boundary segment, so local f f commutator contacts have zero null-channel weight.
All non-endpoint remainders are bounded by a signed tail interval [-tau_end,tau_end] in the same cutoff normalization.
definitions: source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulated endpoint boxes v with local Wilson partition functions Z_{v,a}(J) and the locked Feshbach null incidence vector eta_v.
target object: a certified scalar interval for the post-H,K connected boundary-OPE polarization R_end in the null channel, including endpoint tails.
controlled interface: finite source evaluations L_{v,a}(kh;eta_v)=log Z_{v,a}(kh eta_v) for k=-3,...,3 plus uniform eighth-derivative and tail bounds.

same-theory condition: the sources are only infinitesimal Wilson plaquette-sheet flux insertions generated by the original loops; no boundary counterterm, diagonal renormalization change, or enlarged observable algebra is inserted.

equations.label: singlet endpoint cumulant
equations.valid_when: Valid when heat-kernel endpoint sources have finite support inside one endpoint box and L_v is C^4 near zero.

equations.label: seven point fourth derivative stencil
equations.valid_when: Applies after the source line s eta is fixed and all seven source values lie inside the analyticity interval.

equations.label: stencil certification error
equations.valid_when: Requires eight source derivatives bounded uniformly on the closed segment between the largest positive and negative probe strengths.

equations.label: straight commutator contact cancellation
equations.valid_when: Valid when the regulator assigns the same heat-kernel profile to oppositely oriented plaquette sheets on each straight boundary edge.

equations.label: endpoint R interval
equations.valid_when: Applies after Wick-square disconnected contractions are removed by the connected log and endpoint tails are bounded in the same cutoff scheme.

equations.label: promotion or falsifier test
equations.latex: M_G+\inf\mathcal I_R\ge0\Rightarrow \text{endpoint block passes},\qquad M_G+\sup\mathcal I_R<0\Rightarrow \text{valid falsifier}
equations.valid_when: Requires the already computed H,K Schur-Feshbach margin M_G and an interval enclosing every connected post-H,K endpoint contribution.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: It fails if the seven source values are not same-theory Wilson insertions, if M_8 or tau_end is too singular to certify the interval, or if the interval gives a negative valid falsifier against M_G.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma turns the remaining R problem into a finite, scalar, regulator-level computation in the actual Feshbach null channel, avoiding both the full endpoint spectrum and the old symbolic threshold.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator, the post-H,K endpoint contribution in the Feshbach null channel is certified by scalar fourth source differences of log Z_v. A seven-point stencil improves the previous h^2 M_6 uncertainty to h^4 M_8, while the Gaussian/Wick and straight f f contacts cancel before the sign test.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if same-theory source insertion fails, straight f f cancellation fails, or the certified interval proves M_G+sup I_R<0.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if character expansion, cluster bounds, or computation gives M_G+inf I_R>=0 uniformly through the cutoff-removal scaling window.
control_decision.reason: This is a contribution-making move toward the post-H,K R term: it gives a concrete regulator, cumulant, cancellation, error bound, and promotion/falsifier inequality.

dependency_updates.description: Replaced the endpoint negative-spectrum task by a scalar null-channel cumulant certificate using seven source values of log Z_v.
The regulator is now tied to source derivatives of local endpoint box partition functions and to the straight-edge f f cancellation identity.
Only its null-channel margin M_G enters the endpoint sign test; no further obstruction-ladder restatement is needed.
Must verify that s eta source insertions are infinitesimal deformations of the locked Wilson plaquette sheets, not a new boundary observable.

falsifiers: A certified interval with M_G+sup I_R<0 is a same-theory endpoint falsifier for the finite Wilson block.
Failure of the straight-edge incidence identity in the chosen heat-kernel plaquette geometry revives the f f contact and invalidates the cancellation.
An M_8 bound growing so fast that h^4 M_8 dominates M_G prevents a valid sign certificate before cutoff removal.
If source differentiation of log Z_v requires a boundary counterterm not generated by the original Wilson loops, the same-theory condition is falsified.
Long-range endpoint tails with negative sign larger than the certified local margin would demote the branch even if each local endpoint box passes.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: The next R contribution is scalar. After contracting with the Feshbach null vector, the connected endpoint kappa_4 can be certified from seven same-theory source evaluations of log Z_v with error 7 h^4 M_8/240. The connected log kills Wick-square pieces, the null incidence kills straight f f contacts, and only endpoint/corner cumulants plus tails remain. The branch is not looping; the decisive valid test is the interval sign of M_G+R_end.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute L_{v,a}(kh;eta_v) for k=-3,...,3 in the endpoint heat-kernel character expansion, bound M_{8,v}(3h) and tau_end, then report the certified interval for M_G+R_end.
